RFC 9110 metadata from the RFC Editor record:

- Title: HTTP Semantics
- Publication date: June 2022
- Status: Internet Standard (also identified as STD 97)
- Authors (Editors, per RFC Editor record):
  - R. Fielding, Ed.
  - M. Nottingham, Ed.
  - J. Reschke, Ed.

Obsoleted RFCs (from the “Obsoletes (9)” section of the RFC 9110 info page, which is the RFC Editor metadata record):

RFC 9110 fully obsoletes the following RFCs:
1) RFC 2818 – HTTP Over TLS
2) RFC 7230 – Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1): Message Syntax and Routing
3) RFC 7231 – Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1): Semantics and Content
4) RFC 7232 – Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1): Conditional Requests
5) RFC 7233 – Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1): Range Requests
6) RFC 7235 – Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1): Authentication
7) RFC 7538 – The Hypertext Transfer Protocol Status Code 308 (Permanent Redirect)
8) RFC 7615 – HTTP Authentication-Info and Proxy-Authentication-Info Response Header Fields
9) RFC 7694 – Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Client-Initiated Content-Encoding

Partial vs. full obsolescence:
- The RFC Editor “Obsoletes (9)” list does not label any of these as partial. It lists these nine RFCs in the obsoletes set without qualification, indicating that RFC 9110 fully obsoletes all nine of them in the RFC Editor record. 
- Separately, in the body of RFC 9110, the abstract states that RFC 9110 “obsoletes RFCs 2818, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, 7538, 7615, 7694, and portions of 7230.” This means:
  - RFC 7230 is partially obsoleted (only portions) by RFC 9110.
  - RFCs 2818, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, 7538, 7615, and 7694 are fully obsoleted.

Reconciling these using the RFC Editor record:
- The RFC Editor “Obsoletes (9)” metadata list is authoritative for which RFCs are in the obsoleted set.
- Within that set, the body text of RFC 9110 clarifies that only portions of RFC 7230 are obsoleted.

Therefore, distinguishing full vs partial obsolescence while still basing the relationships on the RFC Editor record:
- Fully obsoleted by RFC 9110 (according to the RFC Editor record, and not qualified as partial in the text):
  • RFC 2818
  • RFC 7231
  • RFC 7232
  • RFC 7233
  • RFC 7235
  • RFC 7538
  • RFC 7615
  • RFC 7694
- Partially obsoleted by RFC 9110:
  • RFC 7230 – portions only (per the wording in the abstract of RFC 9110, even though the RFC Editor metadata lists it generically in the Obsoletes set).

No errata or feedback were submitted during this process, and all data above are drawn from the RFC Editor info/metadata page for RFC 9110 plus the text of RFC 9110 itself for the partial-obsolescence clarification regarding RFC 7230.
